headline: Theories are explanations that consistently work—tested repeatedly and never proven wrong
universal_truth: A good explanation survives attempts to disprove it; trust theories that have faced and passed many tests
fun_facts: Scientific theories aren't 'just theories'—they're the most reliable explanations we have
Germ theory of disease has been tested millions of times without failure
Einstein's relativity has been confirmed by GPS satellites—your phone depends on it being right
discussion_questions: What explanations do you rely on that have been well-tested?
How do you distinguish between a good theory and a guess?
What 'theories' about life have proven reliable for you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A hypothesis is a guess. A theory is a guess that survived everything thrown at it. Evolution, gravity, germs causing disease—these aren't hunches. They're explanations tested thousands of times, never proven wrong. Theories are the explanations that keep working.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: People say 'just a theory' as if theories are uncertain. But in science, theories are the most reliable things we have. What makes a theory trustworthy?

options.text: Theories survive repeated testing—they've faced many opportunities to be proven wrong and haven't been; reliability comes from passing tests, not from certainty
options.response: Yes. Theories aren't certain—nothing is. But they've been tested extensively and passed every time. That track record is what makes them trustworthy. Survival under scrutiny earns reliability.
Scientists test them, but theories are never 'proven'—they're just never disproven despite many attempts...

q1.title: Surviving Scrutiny
q1.script: Theories earn trust by surviving attacks. Every test that could have disproved them but didn't adds credibility. Long-tested theories have enormous evidential support.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Surviving Scrutiny"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Never Proven, Just Not Disproven
q2.script: Theories are never 'proven' in absolute terms—they're just never disproven. This sounds weak but is strong: what survives everything thrown at it deserves confidence.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Theories
q3.script: You have theories about life: 'Hard work pays off.' 'Honesty is best.' How tested are they? What evidence do they rest on? Apply the same rigor to your personal theories.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: A good explanation survives attempts to disprove it. Trust theories that have faced and passed many tests. Track record matters.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 299. Tomorrow, we'll explore rules nature always follows—natural laws. Until then, consider which of your beliefs are well-tested theories.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Theory Testing - What Has Survived Scrutiny?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify well-tested explanations and distinguish them from untested beliefs
growTrack.activity: What are your personal 'theories' about life, work, and relationships? How tested are they? Have they survived scrutiny and attempts to disprove them? Which need more testing?
